During the second operation, another drone was launched but crashed inside the post. The soldiers approached the downed aircraft and, for reasons that remain unclear, it exploded.
Both soldiers received medical treatment at the scene before being evacuated by helicopter in critical condition to a hospital in Israel, where they were pronounced dead.
The military has opened an investigation into the incident and said all possibilities were being examined, including whether communications interference may have contributed to the malfunction.
Pending the findings of the investigation, the IDF has suspended use of the drone model involved in the explosion.
The deaths were the latest fatalities involving Israeli personnel operating in Gaza. In June, Raad Abu al-Qi'an, a resident of the Bedouin town of Hura who worked in Gaza as a civilian contractor for the Defense Ministry, was killed when a building collapsed in Jabaliya.
Civilian contractors working on behalf of the military are not recognized as fallen IDF soldiers. After their deaths, they receive the more limited designation of victims of hostile acts rather than recognition as fallen members of the IDF and security forces.
Before Thursday's incident, the most recent IDF fatality in Gaza was Staff Sgt. Ofri Yafe, a Paratroopers Brigade soldier from Moshav Hayogev in the Jezreel Valley, who was killed by friendly fire in Khan Younis on Feb. 18.

Chinese brands are scarce on Washington’s streets, so are the CEOs in Trump-Xi summit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
05:30:00 UTC
14:30:00 KST

No BYD or Luckin: The curious absence of China brands in Washington and at White House state dinner
- Chinese consumer brands were largely absent from Washington, highlighting limited Chinese business presence in the US capital.
- Xi Jinping's visit focused mainly on political issues, with no accompanying Chinese business delegation, contrasting with Trump's earlier Beijing visit with many US executives.
- US restrictions and tensions create investment challenges, causing cautious attitudes towards Chinese products despite their growing global influence and consumer use in the US.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – In the streets of the US capital, signs of China’s growing consumer clout can be surprisingly hard to find.
There are no BYD electric cars cruising down Pennsylvania Avenue; instead, Japanese auto brands Honda, Toyota and Subaru are a far more common sight. Huawei or Xiaomi phones, two major Chinese tech brands, are not spotted in people’s hands. And Chinese chains such as Luckin Coffee and Haidilao hotpot that have opened in other US cities have no presence in Washington.
What is easily recognisable in Washington, however, is Pop Mart, the Beijing-founded toy company behind the popular Labubu figurines. But even its nearest store is across the Potomac River in Arlington, Virginia, where it opened in 2025, although another store is slated to open in the district of Georgetown.
Meanwhile, boba fans have to venture even farther afield to Rockville, Maryland, a suburb with a sizeable Asian-American population north-west of Washington, for a sip of China’s new-style teas from Molly Tea and Heytea.
The relative absence is striking at a time when Chinese consumer brands, from electric cars and smartphones to collectible toys and fashion brands, are expanding rapidly in markets elsewhere around the world.
And on Sept 24, that absence extended all the way to the White House.
At a state dinner held by US President Donald Trump in honour of Chinese President Xi Jinping, the guest list featured a who’s who of corporate America.
Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Advanced Micro Devices’ Lisa Su, Apple’s Tim Cook and Tesla’s Elon Musk sat at the same table with Trump, Xi and their spouses.
According to the official White House dinner guest list, only 19 of the 134 were from the Chinese side, which included Xi and other top officials such as Xi’s chief of staff Cai Qi, Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, Vice-Premier He Lifeng and Chinese Ambassador to the US Xie Feng.
Xi had arrived in Washington on Sept 23 without a business delegation, despite rumours of plans being drawn up as recently as a week before his visit for Chinese executives from some of China’s biggest companies to accompany him.
Reuters had previously reported that representatives from electric car giant BYD, smartphone company Xiaomi, battery makers CATL and Gotion, consumer electronics manufacturer Hisense, automotive parts company Wanxiang, state-owned Bank of China and agricultural conglomerate COFCO Group were among those under consideration.
In contrast, when Trump visited Beijing in May, more than a dozen US business leaders, including Musk, Cook, Huang, Citigroup’s Jane Fraser, Goldman Sachs’ David Solomon and Boeing’s Kelly Ortberg, went along. Several went on to meet senior Chinese officials and regulators on their own after the presidential summit.
Who’s not there: Does it matter?
The absence of Chinese business titans on Xi’s trip to Washington should not be over-interpreted, said Zhang Yun, an international relations professor at Nanjing University.
He said that Xi’s unusually tight three-day itinerary, confined to Washington, meant that the visit was primarily focused on political and strategic issues, while business engagement could potentially be left for another occasion.
He pointed to Xi’s first state visit in 2015, where 15 Chinese business honchos, including Alibaba’s Jack Ma, Tencent’s Pony Ma, Baidu’s Robin Li and Lenovo’s Yang Yuanqing, attended a US-China business roundtable in Seattle. The business leaders did not follow Xi on the Washington leg of his visit to meet then President Barack Obama.
One opportunity for China and the US to talk business could come as soon as the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen in November, where Xi and Trump could meet again, said Zhang.
“After all, Shenzhen is a window into China’s reform and opening up, and its new and high-technology industries,” he added.
George Chen, a partner and co-chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, similarly cautioned against interpreting the lopsided corporate turnout as a barometer of the summit’s success, as their absence carries little bearing.
For Trump, assembling some of America’s biggest technology executives served to showcase US competitiveness and innovation, particularly in artificial intelligence.
But for Xi, having a matching contingent of Chinese executives was “nice to have, but not necessary”, he added.
“For the Chinese political system, it is always about the party, about the ruler, rather than about how much influence the business community can have,” Chen said, pointing to Beijing’s previous crackdown on its technology sector and what he described as the government’s “mixed relationship” with the industry.
Nanjing University’s Zhang said the more consequential issue was not whether Chinese executives were seated at the White House dinner, but the difficult environment for investment between the world’s two largest economies.
“This is particularly the case with Chinese investment in the US, which faces all kinds of US restrictions, including those imposed on national security grounds and security reviews, which have created many difficulties and obstacles for Chinese investment,” Zhang said.
Huawei has, for years, faced sweeping US restrictions on its telecommunications equipment and access to American technology, while CATL and Gotion have come under scrutiny in Washington over national security and alleged military links.
Meanwhile, BYD has effectively been shut out of the US passenger electric vehicle market by steep tariffs and other restrictions on Chinese-made vehicles and technology.
While Trump has said he welcomes Chinese investment, Zhang said: “Rhetoric is not the same as institutionalised arrangements.
“That is why interaction between the Chinese and US presidents is important in providing a more predictable environment and greater certainty for businesses on both sides to invest in each other’s countries.”
Beyond government policies, uncertainty over economic ties with China can also be felt at the consumer level.
Near the White House, a 24-year-old US federal worker, who declined to give her name as she works for the government, described her relationship with Chinese technology as one of “keeping a safe distance”.
“There is that inherent worry of data leakage and privacy infringement, especially on platforms where you have to input your financial details,” she said, explaining why she deliberately stays away from platforms such as Temu and Shein, both popular online shopping sites.
However, TikTok, her social media platform of choice, proved harder to give up.
When the app briefly went offline in the US in January 2025, she switched to Instagram Reels and initially stayed away even after TikTok returned. But she eventually went back.
“Regardless of whether Americans want to or not, so many of the products we use without realising it are of Chinese origin,” she said.
“So, I think it is more just a matter of practicality than it is a matter of principle.”

Frida Escobedo Studio to Design Underground Expansion for Buenos Aires' MALBA Museum
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
05:30:00 UTC
14:30:00 KST

Amid the celebrations marking the 25th anniversary of the Buenos Aires Museum of Latin American Art (MALBA), the institution confirmed the museum's expansion beneath Plaza Perú, which will double its exhibition space. The architects selected for the project are New York- and Mexico City-based Taller Frida Escobedo, who presented the project at the anniversary gala. The studio has previous experience with cultural architecture and is also currently developing the Centre Pompidou renovation project led by Moreau Kusunoki, as well as a new wing of the Met Museum in New York. The MALBA expansion includes new temporary exhibition halls, a new auditorium, multipurpose spaces, an outdoor plaza-courtyard, workshops, storage areas, and offices, and is scheduled to open in late 2029 or early 2030.
The studio's narrative for the project begins with the museum's history: a collection that became an institution, an institution that progressively expanded to include film, literature, education, and public programs. Now, on the occasion of its 25th anniversary, the new objective is to transform the museum's relationship with the city by changing the way the building is visited and inhabited. The need for expansion stems from another celebratory event: the recent addition of the Daros Latinamerica Collection, which brings new Latin American art from the second half of the twentieth century, as well as contemporary art. Within this need for expansion, Frida Escobedo's studio is taking the opportunity to transform the museum as a whole, connecting existing spaces to allow current programs to develop further and to activate the relationship with the adjacent Plaza República del Perú.
The current museum building does not have a carefully crafted relationship with its immediate urban surroundings. The underground design of the expansion, beneath the plaza, makes it possible to create a new relationship without reducing the park's area, giving MALBA a new urban dimension and culturally activating the plaza. The entire perimeter of the building will also be transformed to open up relationships with the street. A new sculpture garden, the central courtyard, new entrances, and connections with Plaza República del Perú will allow the museum to be approached from different directions, linking the existing building, the expansion, and the park.
Related Article
Buenos Aires Architecture Biennial Celebrates 40 Years With a Free Program Under the Theme of Inhabiting
The intervention begins by clearing the building's center, currently constrained by the intensity and diversity of the museum's uses. The space extends downward into the subsoil, connecting the existing building with the extension and freeing up the central space for gathering, circulation, and display. The design aims to create a common thread between the museum's different cultural activities. The new exhibition halls will coexist with spaces specifically designed for film, literature, education, and public programs. The auditorium and multipurpose spaces, meanwhile, can be visited along a continuous path or operate independently, allowing a screening, a talk, an educational activity, or an event to take place simultaneously or outside regular opening hours, broadening the museum's offerings to the city.
Other recent announcements about museums include the expansion and adaptive reuse of several historic structures at the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland. The expansion extends the existing museum, designed by Renzo Piano, with three new buildings by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor. Earlier this week, the long-awaited Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, designed by MAD Architects, opened its doors to the public in Los Angeles, United States. Danish architecture practice AART has won the international competition for Rigets Skatkammer (The Royal Treasury), a new 1,300-square-meter underground extension to the museum at Rosenborg Castle in Copenhagen.

Two IDF soldiers were killed when a drone that they were operating landed and exploded within their military outpost in the northern Gaza Strip, the military said on Friday.
The soldiers, who were reservists serving as part of the 16th Brigade, were initially evacuated to Barzilai Medical Center in Ashkelon but were pronounced dead, 99th Division Chief Brig.-Gen. Elad Tzuri said.
The two soldiers were Maj. (Res.) Nadav Kali, 24, from Har Halutz, and Maj. (Res.) Ofek Moalem, 23, from Jerusalem.
The soldiers were operating a drone, successfully completing their first operation, Tzuri noted.
However, during the second operation, the drone crashed within their outpost in the northern Gaza Strip. The two soldiers went to investigate the crash site, at which time the drone exploded, Tzuri said.
The two were "excellent soldiers," Tzuri said, highlighting that one was a sergeant and the other a squad commander.
The 16th Brigade had been operating in this area of the northern Gaza Strip since September 10, Tzuri clarified.
No other soldiers were wounded in the incident, Tzuri added.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu mourned the fallen soldiers, stating that he and his wife joined all of Israel in grieving them.
"Nadav and Ofek, of blessed memory, were brave reserve soldiers who defended Israel's security," he said. "We embrace their families in their difficult hour and send them our deepest condolences."
Defense Minister Israel Katz also shared his condolences for the two fallen soldiers in a post on X/Twitter.
"At the hour when the people of Israel is preparing for the holiday, two dear families are grappling with the worst of all," Katz wrote.
"On behalf of the entire security establishment, I wish to embrace and send condolences from the depths of the heart to their families. May the memory of Nadav and Ofek be a blessing."
IDF investigating whether Hamas responsible for incident
The IDF is investigating whether Hamas utilized the electromagnetic spectrum to bring down the drone. The IDF currently believes that Hamas lacks the operational capability in the spectrum domain to carry out such a maneuver.
The investigation is also examining how the explosive device detonated as the two soldiers approached the drone. The IDF declined to specify whether it was a suicide drone or a drone designed to drop munitions.
The IDF has grounded all attack and munition-dropping drones across all combat sectors pending the outcome of the investigation into this serious incident.

The coalition bloc fell by one seat to just 49 as both haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties lost one seat each, according to a Maariv poll published on Friday.
The poll also found that Otzma Yehudit gained one seat, rising to nine, while Likud remained at 18 seats, Religious Zionism-Zehut at six, and People of Israel at four.
In the opposition bloc, Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar continued its downward trend, losing another seat this week to stand at 22.
Elsewhere in the bloc, the Democrats gained two seats to reach 11, while B’Yachad remained at 13 and Yisrael Beytenu at nine. The joint Reservists-Economic Party remained at four seats, while the Arab parties also remained unchanged with a combined 12 seats. Overall, the Zionist opposition bloc gained one seat, rising to 55.
Meanwhile, Blue and White, led by Benny Gantz, received 1.3% of the vote; the Haredi Public party, led by Moti Leitner, received 0.9%; and Noam for Israel, led by Avi Maoz, received 0.7%. None crossed the electoral threshold.
Asked which party they would vote for if Knesset elections were held now, respondents gave Yashar! 22 seats, Likud 18, B’Yachad 13, the Democrats 11, Yisrael Beytenu nine, Otzma Yehudit nine, the Joint Arab List seven, United Torah Judaism six, Shas six, Religious Zionism-Zehut six, Ra’am five, People of Israel four, and the Reservists-Economic Party four.
Eisenkot, Bennett leading Netanyahu for prime minister
The Maariv poll also found that Eisenkot continued to lead Benjamin Netanyahu in a head-to-head question on suitability to serve as prime minister, with an eight-percentage-point advantage. Eisenkot received 47% support, compared with 39% for Netanyahu.
Naftali Bennett also led Netanyahu, receiving 46% compared with Netanyahu’s 42%. Avigdor Liberman, meanwhile, narrowed the gap with Netanyahu to three percentage points, with Netanyahu receiving 43% and Liberman 40%.
The survey also found that nearly half of opposition party voters, 48%, would prefer the party leaders to announce now that the head of whichever opposition list wins the most seats would become their candidate for prime minister.
About a quarter, 23%, said the bloc should decide and announce now who its candidate for prime minister will be. Another 18% preferred to leave the decision until after the election, while 11% said they did not know.
About one-third of Israelis, 34%, said they want Netanyahu to serve as prime minister after the election, driven in large part by the fact that 82% of coalition bloc voters chose him.
Among opposition party voters, Eisenkot was the leading choice, with 50% saying they wanted him to be the next prime minister. Bennett followed with 25% support among opposition bloc voters, followed by Yair Lapid with 11%, Netanyahu with 5%, and Liberman with 3%.
Broken down by support for individual opposition parties, most voters chose the leader of their preferred party as their candidate for prime minister. Support for Eisenkot among Yashar voters, at 88%, was higher than the 78% support Bennett received among B’Yachad voters.
Majority of Israelis unconcerned about international standing
The Maariv poll further found that a majority of Israelis, 62%, were concerned about what the survey described as Israel’s low standing internationally. Another 31% said they were not concerned, while 7% had no opinion.
A clear divide emerged between coalition and opposition voters. A majority of coalition voters, 59%, said they were not concerned, while an overwhelming 88% of opposition voters said they were concerned, including 54% who said they were very concerned.
The poll was conducted by Lazar Research, headed by Dr. Menachem Lazar, in cooperation with Panel4ALL, on Wednesday and Thursday, September 23-24. A total of 4,217 people were invited to participate, with 610 respondents, or 14%, completing the survey. The respondents constituted a representative sample of Israel’s adult population aged 18 and over, including Jews and Arabs. The poll had a maximum sampling error of 4%.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan will hold an urgent, high-level meeting under a joint defense pact to discuss ways to support the kingdom amid attacks by Yemen's Houthis, while Saudi's top religious authority told troops to be ready to lay down their lives to fight their Iran-aligned enemy.
The Houthis have launched strikes on the Saudi-backed government in Yemen and repeatedly fired into Saudi Arabia, disrupting oil flows from the world's largest energy exporter, as part of a wider Middle East war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets on Thursday, while authorities in Saudi Arabia said they had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Houthi fighters.
Turkey's Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will travel to Saudi Arabia to meet his Saudi and Pakistani counterparts as part of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, the Defense Ministry said on Friday.
Saudi Arabia earlier had issued emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red Sea oil port.
Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti, the kingdom's top religious authority, called on soldiers to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Houthis until the group is ousted from power, according to a statement posted by the Saudi state news agency late on Thursday.
Amid the fighting, the Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, according to a Saudi foreign ministry statement. They condemned the attacks targeting Mecca and other civilian sites, while affirming Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself, the statement said.
"The ministers also discussed arrangements for holding an urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries to discuss ways to support Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which stipulates that an attack against any one of the parties constitutes an attack against all parties," the statement said.
The meeting was announced shortly after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sought to distance Iran from the Houthis in an American television interview on Thursday.
"The Houthis are responsible for their own actions," Pezeshkian told the Fox News program "Special Report with Bret Baier" a day after he appeared before the UN General Assembly in New York.
US-Iran diplomacy attempts
The Pezeshkian interview and speech took place amid a pause in fighting between the US and Iran and a brief attempt at diplomacy in New York, with Qatar serving as an intermediary between the warring parties.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters on Thursday that Tehran had conveyed a proposal to the United States via intermediaries under which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened if Tehran’s conditions were met.
Under Iran’s proposal, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, within seven days. The United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, he said.
“The Strait of Hormuz will be reopened on the last day,” Araqchi said, adding that talks with the United States on other issues, including Iran’s nuclear issue, would then start.
Tehran reviewing Washington's response to peace proposals
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals.
Oil prices fell on Friday as markets weighed the possibility of a truce, even as the number of ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz dropped to nine on Thursday, half the 10-day average.
The war, which US President Donald Trump launched alongside Israel in February, has killed thousands of people and disrupted global energy supplies.
While the US and Iran have largely stood down from direct combat, Iranian allies are engaged in the region with Hezbollah confronting Israel in Lebanon and the Houthis advancing in Yemen.
Iran and its allies have significantly pressured oil exports from Saudi Arabia, a US ally. The Houthis have disrupted ship traffic at the mouth of the Red Sea while Iran has effectively limited tanker traffic at the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for 20% of the world's oil exports before the start of the war. An attack by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq also temporarily knocked Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline out of service.
Security experts have debated exactly how much Iran directly influences the Houthis, a Shi'ite Islamist movement that evolved from a local insurgency into a powerful armed group controlling much of northern Yemen.
However, Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources have said the Houthis' advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast was carried out with direct guidance from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as "secondary sanctions".
Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries including the UAE and Oman on Thursday in response to new US sanctions, the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in third countries that do business with Iran.
A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea.
"We are living in an open-air prison," a retired teacher in Tehran told Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.

Full text: Xi's remarks at state dinner held by Trump at the White House
China

WASHINGTON, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday gave remarks at the state dinner hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States.
The following is the full text of the remarks:
Honorable President Donald J. Trump and Mrs. Melania Trump,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
Thank you, Mr. President and Mrs. Trump, for extending to my wife and me your gracious hospitality and thoughtful arrangements. You and Mrs. Trump have made many special arrangements for our visit, all prepared with meticulous care and consideration in every detail. You make us feel truly at home. I would also like to extend my sincere greetings to Americans from all sectors of society who care about China-U.S. relations and support the further growth of our bilateral ties. As I speak, my compatriots in China are celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival -- a cherished occasion for family reunion in Chinese tradition. I wish you all a very happy Mid-Autumn Festival, and my best wishes to you and your families.
In May this year, President Trump paid a successful visit to China at my invitation. We agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. During the visit, President Trump warmly invited me to visit the United States, and I have come as promised. In less than half a year, the Chinese and American presidents have exchanged state visits, making history in our bilateral engagement. Today, President Trump and I had sincere and in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues. This has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and provided new strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations.
Not long ago, the United States celebrated the 250th anniversary of its independence. On that occasion, I sent my congratulations on behalf of the Chinese government and people. The past 200-plus years have also witnessed friendly exchanges between China and the United States.
Over 200 years ago, soon after its independence, the United States turned its eyes to China. Our two countries started trading with each other, exchanging goods to meet each other's needs and draw on our complementary strengths. In fact, President George Washington had personally acquired a large collection of Chinese porcelain.
Over 80 years ago, the Chinese and American people stood shoulder to shoulder in the fight against Japanese militarist aggressors. Together we opened the famous Hump air route over the Himalayas. During the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, Chinese soldiers and civilians rescued hundreds of American pilots at the cost of hundreds of thousands of Chinese lives. Such a friendship, forged in blood and fire, will surely live on through the generations.
Over 50 years ago, Ping-Pong Diplomacy between China and the United States reopened the door to bilateral exchanges that had been closed for years. With the political wisdom embodied in "a small ball moving the globe," the older generation of Chinese and American statesmen, led by Chairman Mao Zedong and President Richard Nixon, set in motion the historic process of normalizing relations between our two countries. The redwood trees that President Nixon had presented as a special state gift have taken root in Zhejiang Province where I worked for several years.
Over 20 years ago, an American named Ronald Sakolsky gave financial support to Yin Yuzhen, a Chinese desert control worker, for her tree-planting effort. Just recently, Ronald, now an elderly man, returned to China. He saw with his own eyes that the desert back then had turned into a lush forest. This story touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between our two peoples.
Exchanges have helped promote heart-to-heart communication between our peoples and cemented public support for China-U.S. friendship and cooperation.
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
Reviewing the past gives us new perspectives. Today, we have come to another historic juncture for China-U.S. relations. Together, let us nurture the beautiful flowers of China-U.S. friendship. Together, let us write a new chapter in our friendly relations.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- As Chinese President Xi Jinping and his U.S. counterpart, Donald Trump, met on Thursday at the White House under global gaze, they reached many new common understandings, providing fresh strategic guidance for the world's most important bilateral relationship.
While those common understandings have further enriched the vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, Xi went further by urging the two sides to translate that vision into action and find the right way for the two major countries to get along.
For China and the United States, that means working toward a direction featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace.
There is ample reason to do so. The interests of China and the United States are deeply intertwined, and there is plenty of room for them to work together. Also, achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand.

The same approach can also be applied to emerging areas that will shape the future of humanity. Both China and the United States are leading nations in artificial intelligence (AI). Today, China-U.S. relations once again stand at a new historical starting point. Building a constructive relationship of strategic stability between the two major countries is not an expediency, nor will it be realized overnight. The two sides need to work persistently to deliver on their common understandings and work together to build a better world. ■

China Focus: Beijing Culture Forum highlights closer connection between young people, cultural heritage
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
13:26:16 CST
14:26:16 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- Cultural heritage often conjures images of the distant past: yellowed, crumpled pages, dust-covered artifacts, or centuries-old techniques that seem far removed from younger generations. But Li Ziqi, 36, has a different perspective.
Through her poetic portrayal of rural life and traditional crafts, the Chinese video creator has helped China's cultural heritage reach a global audience, amassing over 30 million YouTube subscribers.
At the 2026 Beijing Culture Forum, held earlier this week in Beijing, Li encouraged everyone, especially young people, to forge a closer bond with cultural heritage. "Culture does not exist solely in museum display cases. It lives in the fabric of everyday life," she said.
Her remarks echoed a broader discussion at the two-day forum, which brought together more than 600 guests from 44 countries and regions to discuss cultural heritage and mutual learning among civilizations.
For the first time since its 2022 debut, this year's event held a parallel forum focused on young people, highlighting their role in cultural heritage protection.
"For a long time, heritage protection was mainly a matter for older people, but young people are the future and should be aware of the importance of heritage," said Leonardo Barci Castriota, vice president of the International Council on Monuments and Sites.
While school education is essential to raise young people's awareness, it is also important to make cultural heritage more accessible by providing hands-on experiences beyond the classroom, Adam Green, a senior lecturer in sustainability at the University of York in Britain, told Xinhua.
Green cited a cultural program at York Minster, a historic cathedral, where young people were invited to design their own architectural creations with LEGO bricks, inspired by the building itself.
"It gets children thinking about the material in a creative, proactive, and critical way," he said, adding that such activities can "create an inclusive environment" for young people to engage with heritage resources and generate new visions.
In China, innovative programs are encouraging greater youth involvement in cultural heritage protection, with technology making it easier than ever for young people to take part.
One example is an initiative under the "Digital Central Axis" project, which uses digital tools to protect the Beijing Central Axis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Young people can photograph cultural landmarks along the axis and upload pictures to an online monitoring platform in real time.
To date, the initiative has collected more than 180,000 monitoring photos from nearly 30,000 participants, most aged 10 to 16. It offers young people a simple yet effective way to protect cultural heritage, said Li Wenxuan, head of the "Digital Central Axis" project.
Meanwhile, the forum also put the spotlight on young people pursuing careers in cultural heritage.
Zhong Fangrong, a Gen-Z researcher at the Institute of Archaeology of the Dunhuang Academy, once drew widespread attention on Chinese social media after choosing to study archaeology at Peking University, despite long-standing stereotypes that the field offered limited earning potential, particularly for students from low-income families.
Six years later, Zhong has no regrets over her decision and feels a strong sense of achievement from her excavation and recording work in the caves of Dunhuang, a key hub on the ancient Silk Road in Gansu Province, northwest China.
"What we document may have never been recorded before, but by preserving it today, we may leave something that people a hundred years from now can still draw on," she said.
Zhong is not alone. At the Dunhuang Academy, for example, Ding Xiaohong, deputy director of the Cultural Heritage Digitalization Research Institute, said most members of his team are young people from diverse academic backgrounds.
For young people, simply preserving what has been passed down is just the beginning of the story.
Lang Jiaziyu, a 31-year-old forum participant, is the third-generation inheritor of "Dough Figurine Lang," a folk art recognized as a national intangible cultural heritage (ICH) item in China. He believes that being an inheritor involves more than mastering the craft itself.
"On the one hand, we need to innovate our techniques and incorporate new elements into our works. On the other hand, an important task for our generation is to explore the potential of ICH and unlock its value across different industries," he said.
The tech-savvy inheritor now uses AI, 3D scanning, and other technologies to create short videos about his work and daily life for social media. He also plans to promote the traditional craft through video games and micro dramas.
In addition, Lang has taken his craft abroad through international cultural exchanges, introducing audiences across Asia, Europe and the Americas not only to his intricate figurines but also to the stories and cultural ideas behind them.
"As a young Chinese ICH inheritor, I feel proud and confident to showcase our culture on the global stage," he said.
These efforts cannot be sustained without national support for ICH protection, including policies, funding, and platforms, Lang added.
Li echoed this point at the forum, noting that the government, media, ICH inheritors, online content creators, and supportive netizens are all working together to create a positive environment for young people to grow in the cultural heritage sector.
Recently, China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism released a plan for carrying forward ICH during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). The document specifies major tasks, including strengthening the cultivation of young talent in the sector.
"Whether in the online or offline world, cultural heritage is never carried forward by one person alone. It takes an entire chain of efforts, with every link essential and every part closely connected to the others," she said. ■

Tata v Tata: What’s behind India’s big boardroom brawl?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
05:22:23 UTC
14:22:23 KST

Tata v Tata: What’s behind India’s big boardroom brawl?
India’s most famous conglomerate is knee-deep in feuds over who gets to decide the Tata Group’s future.
New Delhi, India – An unprecedented power struggle has erupted at the top of one of India’s largest conglomerates, pitting the board of its holding company Tata Sons against its majority shareholder Tata Trusts.
Last week, Tata Sons extended Chairman N Chandrasekaran’s term and said it would consider publicly listing the holding company, flying in the face of the family charity that controls the 158-year-old Tata Group.
Extending Chandrasekaran’s chairmanship and taking Tata public is at the heart of the family-linked feud – and its outcome will not be limited merely to the group’s headquarters at Bombay House.
Collectively, listed Tata companies have a market capitalisation of $277bn and influence over 17.7 million retail shareholders apart from pension funds, insurers and mutual funds, investment advisory firm InGovern said.
So what’s behind the bitter brawl inside one of the corporate world’s most consequential boardrooms?
How big is the Tata Group?
The Tata Group business conglomerate spans industries from information technology and automobiles to steel, power, aviation, chemicals and consumer goods.
It has 26 publicly listed companies, including TCS and Tata Motors. They have a combined market capitalisation of $277bn and operate across more than 100 countries. Tata Sons serves as the group’s principal holding and investment company.
The group’s humble beginnings go back more than 150 years when Nusserwanji Tata, born into a Parsi priest’s family in Gujarat, moved to Mumbai (then Bombay) in the mid-19th century and entered the trading business.
He later expanded into trade with China before his son Jamsetji Tata built the business into an industrial group, riding on deals in cotton and opium. Opium was then banned by China’s Qing rulers, and Nusserwanji found a way to smuggle it.
The conglomerate’s real breakthrough came when the United States Civil War broke out in 1861. The disruption to US cotton supplies sent Indian cotton prices soaring and transformed the fortunes of Bombay’s merchants, including the Tatas.
Their businesses turned into an empire over coming generations. Jamsetji Tata died in 1904, and his sons Dorabji and Ratanji Tata carried his businesses forward. The family’s charitable trusts became major shareholders of Tata Sons.
JRD Tata, who became chairman in 1938, transformed the group into a diversified industrial enterprise, expanding into aviation, including India’s flagship carrier, Air India; chemicals; and engineering. In 1991, Ratan Tata succeeded JRD, taking over as India began economic liberalisation.
Under Ratan, the Tata Group consolidated a sprawling group under a more unified corporate identity and pushed it onto the global stage with landmark acquisitions, including Tetley, Corus and Jaguar Land Rover. Tata is now pushing into the next generation of global manufacturing with a major iPhone assembly operation in India and a semiconductor fabrication and chip-assembly business.
Ratan was the chairman of both Tata Sons and its majority stakeholder, Tata Trusts, and remained a bridge between the two. After he died in 2024, a widening schism gradually became apparent.
Tata Trusts is an umbrella of family-linked charities that own 66 percent of Tata Sons.
So what’s Tata v Tata about?
The face-off was triggered on September 17 when Tata Sons reappointed Chandrasekaran as its chairman over the Tata Trusts’ nominee on the board, Noel Tata, in a 4-to-1 vote.
Noel Tata is the sitting chairman of Tata Trusts and the only family-linked senior executive sitting in the top echelons of Tata Sons today. Noel is the half-brother of Ratan Tata and became Tata Trusts’ chairman after Ratan’s death in 2024.
But the divisions between the company and majority shareholder run deeper – and include questions of taking Tata Sons public and providing a planned exit to Tata Sons’ second-largest shareholder, Shapoorji Pallonji.
Chandrasekaran’s reappointment
Last month, Chandrasekaran said he would not seek another term as chairman after February 2027. But Tata Group said in a statement the board asked him to reconsider the group’s “larger interests”, a request that he accepted.
The 68-year-old Noel Tata called the reappointment “illegal” under Tata Sons’ articles of association, adding in a statement that both trust nominees on the board were required to vote in coordination, whereas only Noel Tata voted against. The other trust nominee, Venu Srinivasan, voted in favour of Chandrasekaran’s reappointment.
This matter is now expected to be decided by the courts.
Listing of Tata Sons
India’s central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), requires companies with assets exceeding $10.45bn to publicly list.
Tata Sons tried to skirt the requirements by deregistering as a nonbank finance company. But days before its board meeting this month, the RBI rejected the company’s request, bringing it closer to a public listing.
Tata’s structure is unusual because the holding company at the very top of the empire is at the moment not itself subject to public-market scrutiny, even though many of the companies beneath it are.
At the board meeting, Tata Sons said it would take steps to comply with the RBI’s requirements. But Noel Tata opposed the move, arguing that listing would alter the character of a group that also supports extensive philanthropic activities.
Shapoorji Pallonji’s proposed exit
The Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds an 18.4 percent stake in Tata Sons and is its second-largest shareholder.
The infrastructure and construction conglomerate is knee-deep in debt and is seeking to monetise its shareholding in Tata Sons.
Tata Trusts said Noel Tata tabled a plan to sell a part of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s stake in the holding company worth $2.61bn. Tata Sons has not yet commented on the plan.
Shapoor Mistry, the group’s patriarch, is also Noel Tata’s brother-in-law. The Shapoorji Pallonji Group backs Tata Sons going public and is opposed to Noel’s position.
What does the dispute mean for India’s economy?
The central question in the showdown that is captivating millions of Indians involves the public listing of Tata Sons.
Noel Tata said in a statement that the Tata Group “was conceived as a national service carried on through business”. The unusual privately owned structure of Tata Sons, Noel argued, has allowed the company to remain in the country’s service and “act repeatedly in ways that a purely commercial calculus would not have supported”.
“A listing will destroy its character and strike at the heart of this principle,” Tata Trusts has argued.
However, Santosh Mehrotra, an Indian development economist, told Al Jazeera that Tata Sons needs to be listed publicly, no matter what. “There is a law for everyone, and Tata cannot be an exception to that,” he said.
“We are at a stage as a country when top business houses cannot be allowed to continue to behave in whatever manner they have managed to behave in over the last 100 years,” Mehrotra said.
Mehrotra argued that over the past decade under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India’s top business houses, including the empires of billionaires Gauran Adani and Mukesh Ambani, “have been permitted by the government to grow the concentration of industries across sectors in a historically unprecedented manner”.
“India’s biggest business houses have grown horizontally, capturing all sectors, which have come at the cost of people below them in the pyramid,” Mehrotra said.
“That means that the core inflation is being driven essentially by these handful of businesses because their horizontal and vertical control gives them the ability to mock up prices that are unprecedented in our economy’s history while their profits mount,” he said.
Mehrotra said that while the Tata boardroom drama could be captivating for some, “ordinary Indians’ concerns are rooted in regulating the unchecked growth [of conglomerates] backed by the government.”
InGovern, a governance advisory firm, said in a note that a holding company like Tata Sons that exercises “influence over businesses of such scale cannot reasonably remain outside the governance and transparency expectations increasingly associated with systemically important financial and industrial conglomerates”.
What’s the future of Tata Group?
That is slated to be decided in the courtroom now.
Both sides have lawyered up with some of India’s top legal eagles. Harish Salve, a former solicitor general of India, is leading the Tata Sons legal team while Abhishek Singhvi, a member of parliament from the opposition Indian National Congress party, is representing Tata Trusts.
The Tata Group is no stranger to boardroom tussles and dramas. After Ratan Tata stepped down from the Tata Sons chairmanship in December 2012, Cyrus Mistry was appointed to the top job, becoming the first person from outside the Tata family to lead Tata Sons in decades.
However, differences grew between Mistry and Ratan Tata, who was then still heading Tata Trusts, over strategy, governance and capital allocation. Tata Sons pulled off a stunning coup, removing Mistry as the chairman in October 2016.
Cyrus is the younger brother of Shapoor Mistry and also the brother-in-law of Noel Tata. In bitterly fought legal battles, Cyrus eventually lost his case in 2021 before the Supreme Court. At that time, lawyers Salve and Singhvi found themselves on the same side, fighting for Tata Sons against Mistry.
That judgement upheld “that the affirmative voting rights given to Tata Trusts-nominated directors are legal, valid and a globally accepted corporate norm for majority-trust-held institutions”, said Nitin Potdar, a senior company lawyer based in Mumbai.
Currently, the Tata Sons board has two nominated members from Tata Trusts: Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan. While Noel Tata opposed the reinstatement of Chandrasekaran as the chairman of the holding company, Srinivasan voted in favour.
“Even if the two Tata Trusts nominees give their votes differently, that does not give rise to any [legal] deadlock,” Potdar told Al Jazeera.
Singhvi, who will now represent Noel Tata, wrote in an X post that his reaction to the tussle “is one of sadness and regret that these issues could not be solved amicably”.
“But in the ultimate analysis, fundamental rights of shareholder-owners cannot be nullified in the manner in which they have been,” he wrote. “To stultify shareholder ownership rights would spell doomsday for corporate governance across hundreds of Indian companies.”
“Rupturing the over hundred years of Tata Trust and Tata Sons established hyphenated relationship and divorcing one from the other seems unthinkable,” Singhvi said.

Vietnam, Canada Announce Establishment of Strategic Partnership
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
05:22:00 UTC
14:22:00 KST

Vietnam has elevated its relationship to a Strategic Partnership, as Hanoi’s top leader To Lam paid a state visit to the country – the first ever by a general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV).
During a meeting yesterday in Ottawa, Lam and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the two nations were upgrading the Comprehensive Partnership established in 2017.
Vietnamese state media reported that the two nations “agreed that Vietnam–Canada relations have met all the conditions to enter a new stage of development, characterized by a higher level of political trust, broader and more substantive cooperation, and more closely intertwined interests.”
In a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two sides described themselves as “trusted partners” who were committed to a relationship “grounded in mutual respect for each other’s political system, independence, and sovereignty and territorial integrity” and characterized by “balanced and intertwined interests.”
Although the statement did not use the term, it also referenced their common status as “middle powers” reliant on an international order that is beginning to break down under the pressure of economic protectionism and intensifying geopolitical competition. “As countries with deep integration in the global trading system,” it stated, “Canada and Viet Nam recognize that prosperity depends on rules-based international economic engagements.”
According to the joint statement, the Strategic Partnership is focused on eight primary “pillars” of cooperation: bilateral, regional, and multilateral cooperation; trade and investment; transport and infrastructure; digital technologies and artificial intelligence; energy security; food security; defense and security; and education, culture, and “people-to-people ties.”
It said that these eight pillars “position Canada and Viet Nam to address shared challenges, seize emerging opportunities, and contribute to a more secure, prosperous, and dynamic Indo-Pacific region.”
For Canada, the upgrade to its relationship with Vietnam is consistent with both its recent engagement with Asia and the thrust of the now-famous speech that Carney delivered at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January. During the speech, the Canadian leader cited the “rupture” in the world order, and the need for middle powers to “build a new order that encompasses our values, such as respect for human rights, sustainable development, solidarity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the various states.”
Despite their very different political systems, Vietnam and Canada have a lot in common that predicts a future of potentially fruitful cooperation. Both are middle powers bordering two much more powerful countries – China and the United States – that are locked into an increasingly adversarial relationship.
Trade between the two nations has also increased considerably in recent years, reaching $20.6 billion in two-way trade 2025. Vietnam is now Canada’s largest trading partner in ASEAN, while Canada is Vietnam’s ninth-largest in total. Both are also members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, the free trade pact that was negotiated by the U.S. before President Donald Trump withdrew from the agreement in 2017.
For Vietnam, better relations with Canada is a valuable complement to its omnidirectional foreign policy, which seeks to maintain good relations with key partners among both the West and the “rest.” In the two years since taking over as CPV chief, Lam, who was also appointed state president earlier this year, has been particularly energetic in this regard, elevating eight nations into Vietnam’s circle of Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships, the top tier in its diplomatic hierarchy.
In addition to Canada, Vietnam under Lam’s leadership has also established Strategic Partnerships with Czechia, Finland, Bulgaria, and Belarus.

“Is the cause of Man that of each man? That is what utilitarian ethics has been striving to…”
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
05:19:59 UTC
14:19:59 KST

“Is the cause of Man that of each man? That is what utilitarian ethics has been striving to demonstrate since Hegel; if one wishes to give the word useful a universal and absolute meaning, it is always a question of reabsorbing each man into the bosom of mankind; it is said that despite the weaknesses of the flesh and that particular fear which each one experiences in the face of his particular death, the real interest of each one is mingled with the general interest. And it is true that each is bound to all; but that is precisely the ambiguity of his condition: in his surpassing toward others, each one exists absolutely as for himself; each is interested in the liberation of all, but as a separate existence engaged in his own projects. So much so that the terms “useful to Man,” “useful to this man,” do not overlap. Universal, absolute man exists nowhere.”
– Simone de Beauvoir, The Ethics of Ambiguity

‘We have failed Palestine’ — Ireland’s Martin tells UN
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
04:46:24 UTC
13:46:24 KST

Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin told world leaders at the UN General Assembly on Thursday that the international community had failed Palestinians, warning that continued violence and settlement expansion were undermining prospects for a lasting peace.
Addressing the 81st session of the General Assembly in New York, Martin said the international legal order was under “tremendous strain” and described the denial of fundamental human rights as one of the defining challenges of the era.
“We, the collective international community, have failed Palestine,” Martin said, referring to the continuing suffering of civilians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Martin said the first phase of the Gaza peace plan agreed by Israel and Hamas last October was welcome but had not fundamentally changed conditions on the ground.
He pointed to continued Israeli attacks, restrictions on humanitarian assistance and the ongoing suffering of civilians.
Martin warns two-state solution is being eroded
He also condemned the expansion of illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, saying developments there were damaging prospects for a just and lasting peace.
“What we are witnessing on the ground is a deliberate attempt by some to make the prospect of a two-state solution impossible,” Martin said, citing statements attributed to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposing the establishment of a Palestinian state and Israel’s approval of development in the E1 area.
The UN secretary-general has similarly warned that illegal settlement expansion and other developments in the occupied Palestinian territory are eroding the conditions needed for a viable Palestinian state and called for renewed efforts toward a two-state solution.
Ireland backs international legal accountability
Martin also reaffirmed Ireland’s support for the International Criminal Court, saying there could be “no impunity for war crimes” and calling for measures aimed at undermining the court to be withdrawn.
His remarks came amid broader debate at the UN over Gaza, Palestinian statehood and the future of the two-state solution.
The UN secretary-general has urged an end to the fighting, expanded humanitarian access and compliance with international law.
Martin said the international community would ultimately have to confront the record of what has happened in Gaza, warning that the consequences would carry a lasting moral and political weight.
Ireland has been among the countries advocating for Palestinian rights and a negotiated two-state settlement, while Martin’s address placed the issue at the centre of his appeal for a stronger international commitment to human rights and international law.

MOSCOW, September 25. /TASS/. Russia’s Central Election Commission (CEC) will convene on Friday to establish the final results of elections to the ninth convocation of the Russian parliament’s lower chamber, the State Duma.
The commission will announce the exact distribution of all 450 mandates and sum up the results of over 2,200 lower-level electoral campaigns, also held on September 18-20.
The results of the vote were not immediately announced after the polls closed. CEC Chair Ella Pamfilova said that regional commissions were given time until September 25 to conclusively review all incoming complaints and requests, conduct the necessary inquires and only then establish the official outcomes of the campaigns.
Who will make it into the new Duma?
According to preliminary results, five parties crossed the five-percent threshold: the United Russia party, the Communist Party, LDPR, the New People and A Just Russia.
The 225 seats designated for party lists will be distributed among them. The other half of the State Duma will be determined by the voting results in single-seat constituencies.
The United Russia is poised to form the largest faction. Party Chairman Dmitry Medvedev said on September 24 that it is expected to secure 349 seats in total, according to preliminary allocation: 140 via the federal list and 209 in single-seat constituencies.
If the CEC confirms this distribution, it will mark the largest number of seats won by a single party in a legislative election in the entire modern history of the State Duma. The current record is also held by United Russia, which secured 343 seats in the 2016 elections. In 2021, it got 324 mandates.

Xi attends state dinner held by Trump
China
Unknown Publisher

Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses a welcome banquet at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 24, 2026. Xi on Thursday attended a welcome banquet held by U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
WASHINGTON, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Thursday evening attended a state dinner held by U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, at the White House.
Xi and Peng were warmly greeted by the U.S. presidential couple upon their arrival. The two presidential couples posed for photos and met with guests attending the dinner.
Xi and Trump delivered remarks respectively after the dinner began.
Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes for the Mid-Autumn Festival to Americans from all sectors of society who care about and support the further growth of China-U.S. relations.
Xi noted that Trump paid a successful visit to China in May, and that the two heads of state exchanged state visits within six months, making history in bilateral engagement.
He said common understanding on many issues have been reached during his visit this time, adding new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and providing fresh strategic guidance for bilateral ties.
Xi stressed that over 200 years ago, soon after its independence, the United States turned its eyes to China. The two countries started trading with each other, exchanging goods to meet each other's needs and drawing on their complementary strengths.
Noting that more than 80 years ago, the Chinese and American people stood shoulder to shoulder in the fight against Japanese militarist aggressors, Xi said such a friendship forged in blood and fire will surely live on through the generations.
Over 50 years ago, Ping-Pong Diplomacy between the two countries reopened the door to bilateral exchanges that had been closed for years, Xi said. The older generation of Chinese and U.S. statesmen, with the political wisdom of "a small ball moving the globe," set in motion the historic process of normalizing China-U.S. relations.
Xi said the story of an American named Ronald Sakolsky, who more than 20 years ago gave financial support to Chinese desert control worker Yin Yuzhen for her tree-planting effort, touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between the two peoples.
Xi noted that bilateral exchanges have helped promote heart-to-heart communication between the two peoples and cemented public support for China-U.S. friendship and cooperation.
Today, China-U.S. relations have come to another historical juncture, Xi said.
Trump's pledge to make America great again and China's commitment to achieving great national rejuvenation are both ambitious goals that can surely be mutually reinforcing, he said.
He said China and the United States must act as responsible major countries, meet the expectations of the two peoples, keep pace with the trend of the times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other.
Like a river that never stops flowing, history never stands still, Xi said, adding that the friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise.
The two sides should join hands and move forward side by side, nurture the beautiful flowers of China-U.S. friendship, and write a new chapter in their friendly relations, he added.
The state dinner was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, featuring wonderful performances put on by American artists. ■

Indonesian Minister of Marine Affairs and Fisheries Sakti Wahyu Trenggono delivers a speech during a launching ceremony of a capture fisheries cooperation program between China and Indonesia in Tual, Indonesia, Sept. 24, 2026. China and Indonesia on Thursday launched a capture fisheries cooperation program in Tual, a coastal city in Indonesia's Maluku Province. (Xinhua/Cheng Yiheng)
TUAL, Indonesia, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- China and Indonesia on Thursday launched a capture fisheries cooperation program in Tual, a coastal city in Indonesia's Maluku Province.
More than 100 representatives from the two countries' governments, businesses and local fisheries associations attended the launch ceremony at a prime fishing harbor near the junction of the Banda and Arafura seas. After the launch, several modern Chinese fishing vessels sounded their horns and set out for the open sea.
Li Hongwei, minister counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Indonesia, said at the ceremony that the China-proposed 21st Century Maritime Silk Road, a key component of the Belt and Road Initiative, is highly compatible with Indonesia's Global Maritime Fulcrum strategy. The two sides have been advancing the alignment of strategies, plans, industries and projects to build a maritime community with a shared future, he said.
China is ready to use the launch as an opportunity to strengthen technical cooperation, resource conservation and coordination across the fisheries value chain with Indonesia, Li said.
Indonesian Minister of Marine Affairs and Fisheries Sakti Wahyu Trenggono told Xinhua that the ministry's five blue economy initiatives are aligned with China's vision for sustainable global fisheries. He said Indonesia hopes to deepen cooperation with China in capture fisheries, aquaculture and marine conservation.
More than 90 percent of Maluku Province is covered by sea, and local communities depend heavily on marine and fisheries resources.
The project will improve the value chain for fish landing, cold-chain storage, processing and exports. It is expected to create about 1,100 jobs at sea and on land, while also spurring supporting investment in ship repair, cold storage, quality testing and skills training, according to project information. ■

“[The shooter] had the means, the mechanism, and the motive to perpetrate a greater act. EU seeking to curb Russian athletes’ return to international competitions – media
The EU is considering measures to curb the return of Russian and Belarusian athletes to international sports under their national flags following a decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to ease restrictions, Euractiv reported on Thursday, citing EU diplomats.
The proposals were outlined by the EU diplomatic service and the European Commission in a non-paper and have yet to become a formal EC proposal, according to the outlet.
Measures under discussion include targeted sanctions and visa restrictions against individuals linked to Russian and Belarusian sports. Brussels is also considering using EU funding as leverage by restricting financial support for organizations that allow athletes from the two countries to compete under their national symbols.
Another option would seek to curb media revenues linked to Russian athletes, although diplomats have acknowledged that the measure could be difficult to implement. The EU could also approach third countries in an effort to discourage them from facilitating the return of Russian and Belarusian competitors under their national flags.
The proposals have already faced resistance within the bloc. Slovakia blocked a draft set of conclusions discussed by EU security ambassadors on Tuesday, Euractiv reported, citing three diplomats. EU governments reportedly remain divided over how far they should intervene in decisions traditionally made by independent sports federations.
The Commission and the EU diplomatic service are expected to develop further proposals ahead of an EU ministerial meeting on education, sport and culture on November 20.
The discussions follow the IOC’s July decision to provisionally lift restrictions on the Russian and Belarusian Olympic committees, potentially opening the way for their athletes to compete at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics under national symbols. The IOC has said decisions concerning flags, anthems and other national identification at future Games will be made later.
Russian and Belarusian athletes were barred from many international competitions after the Ukraine conflict escalated in February 2022, although a number of sports federations have since eased restrictions.
Russian athletes have subsequently secured several major international titles. In July, 19-year-old Pavel Graudyn won the men’s individual saber title at the World Fencing Championships in Hong Kong.
In August, Evgeniia Chikunova won the women’s 200-meter breaststroke at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, setting a championship record of 2:19.32 while competing under neutral status.
